ArcMeter is a metered payment channel for software that pays per second. A consumer agent opens a channel with a deposit and a rate per second; the provider agent withdraws whatever has accrued at any time; the consumer closes and gets the unspent remainder back. Accrual is capped by the deposit, so a channel can never overdraw, and a second withdrawal in the same second reverts instead of paying twice.

I used Arc Studio as the workspace: the contract and the 12-test Foundry suite were placed and run inside the Studio sandbox (log in media/arc-studio-test-run.txt, project at studio.arc.io/app/c49231bf-9c51-4b97-bd09-7ea77397de3c). Studio refuses to deploy to mainnet, so the deployment and the four demo transactions were signed in the builder wallet itself; every receipt was then re-read from the public Arc RPC and saved in the repo.
